original_question: Study the dynamics and bifurcations of systems with a small number of point vortices on manifolds such as half-planes, quarter-planes, hemispheres, quarter-spheres, disks, tori, cylinders, and half-cylinders.
target_in_paper: Section 10.2 (Finite-dimensional approximations), Problem 28: the open problem asking for a detailed study of the motion and bifurcations of small-N point-vortex dynamics on the listed manifolds. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target: it concerns point-vortex motion/dynamics, bifurcations, a small number of vortices, and essentially the same explicit list of manifolds that appears in Problem 28. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
missing_details: The intended setting is the finite-dimensional Hamiltonian/Kirchhoff point-vortex model used as an approximation to the 2D Euler equation, not an arbitrary vortex PDE or a generic dynamical system on manifolds. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The paper does not fix the exact number of vortices; it deliberately says only a "small number," so the refined question should keep N small and unspecified rather than commit to N = 2, 3, or any other exact value. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The official formulation asks to study both the motion and the bifurcations "in detail"; your draft says dynamics and bifurcations, which is close, but slightly less literal. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The manifold list in Problem 28 is an explicit target list, not merely a few examples introduced by "such as"; to stay faithful, the listed manifolds should be named directly. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

No special circulation constraints (such as zero total vorticity or zero momentum) belong to Problem 28 itself; those appear only in the preceding survey of special integrable cases and should not be inserted into the question. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

Non-orientable surfaces are not part of this formal problem statement; they are mentioned immediately afterward as a separate direction and then formalized in Problem 29, so they should not be folded into the refined question. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

There are no ambient field/ring, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, operator-polynomial, or "for all sufficiently large m" conditions here; this is a geometric/Hamiltonian dynamics problem, so importing such algebraic metadata would be unfaithful. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
refined_question: Within the finite-dimensional Hamiltonian (Kirchhoff) point-vortex models that arise as approximations to the 2D Euler equation, study in detail the motion and bifurcation structure of systems with a small, unspecified number N of point vortices on each of the manifolds explicitly singled out in the paper: the half-plane, quarter-plane, hemisphere, quarter-sphere, disk, torus, cylinder, and half-cylinder.
justification: The draft matches Section 10.2, Problem 28, almost exactly. The nearby discussion first sets the point-vortex context by describing finite-dimensional Hamiltonian approximations to 2D Euler, including known integrable and non-integrable cases on the plane, sphere, torus, half-plane, and quadrant; only then does the paper pose Problem 28 about studying motion and bifurcations on the listed manifolds. The sentence immediately after Problem 28 and the next formal problem separate the non-orientable case, so adding Möbius band, projective plane, or Klein bottle would broaden the question beyond the paper's actual target. The refined wording therefore keeps the scope narrow, makes the point-vortex/Kirchhoff setting explicit, preserves the paper's intentionally unquantified "small number" language, and avoids adding circulation constraints or other hypotheses not present in Problem 28. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
